title: The path check validates where you point; the filesystem object decides where you land: a committed symlink makes the write follow it out of the sandbox
index_line: T-0066 · EXEC · the requested path is legitimately in-repo so validation passes; the symlink already committed routes the write to .git/config (sshCommand) · go · corroborated
invariant_violated: A path-validation check proves where you pointed, not where the write lands. The API validated that the requested path was inside the repository — but Git legitimately stores symlinks, and the filesystem, not the validator, chooses the destination when a write follows one.

mechanism.does: a user with repository rights commits a symlink into a repo they control, its target pointing outside the worktree (e.g. the server-side .git/config)
the file-modification API validates the requested path, which is legitimately inside the repository, so the traversal guard passes
the check validated the path string, never the file it names — the entry is a pointer to an out-of-tree destination
the API writes attacker bytes through the symlink, overwriting the out-of-tree target
the overwritten file is .git/config: its core.sshCommand executes attacker commands at the next git operation

source.file.name.value: a symlink committed as an ordinary git object — the name is legal, the file it names is the escape hatch

source.http.body.value: the file-modification API call supplying the bytes to write

guard.resolve-check.value: the traversal validation added after the earlier path-traversal fix — correct for strings, blind to symlinks

sink.file.write.value: the write-through-symlink into the out-of-tree target (.git/config in the observed chain)

preconditions.expr: the file-modification API checks the requested path but not the resolved target of an existing entry
any account with repository-creation rights (open registration was the default in the observed campaign)
the service is reachable and the repo web UI/API answers

success: a write to an in-repo path lands outside the repository root
.git/config gains core.sshCommand; the next git fetch/push executes it
campaign signature: fresh repos with random 8-character names holding a single symlink (700+ of ~1,400 exposed instances compromised in the wild)
failure_like: the API resolves the final target (EvalSymlinks/openat per component) and refuses the write
false_positive: a ../ traversal is the older CVE-2024-55947 mechanism — this record requires an in-repo path whose resolved target escapes
reading through a symlink without a write is not this record

hazards: every 'edit a file in the repo' API — git-forge forks inherit the symlink semantics; wiki and attachment writers too
fix discipline from the patch review: O_NOFOLLOW only guards the trailing component — full safety needs openat() walking every component from the root
this class regresses: Gogs repeated it (CVE-2024-56731, CVE-2024-54148); each new write path (rename, merge, rebase) re-opens it
writes into config a privileged process honors (.git/config sshCommand, hook files) convert an out-of-tree write into execution
non_transfers: repositories that reject symlinks at receive time
APIs that only ever create new files (never follow existing entries)

evidence.target: Gogs < 0.13.4 (CVE-2025-8110; mass exploitation July 2025, fix v0.13.4 on 2026-01-23)

provenance.author: Wiz Research (Gili Tikochinski, Yaara Shriki)
provenance.corroborates: the full chain: commit a symlink, PutContents writes through it out of the repo, .git/config sshCommand executes; open registration default; 700+ of ~1,400 exposed instances compromised; fix v0.13.4

provenance.author: oss-security thread (Jakub Wilk)
provenance.corroborates: community tracking of the disclosure and the fork exposure question (Gitea/Forgejo)

provenance.author: oss-security thread (Michael Orlitzky, Collin Funk)
provenance.corroborates: independent mechanism review of the fix: O_NOFOLLOW guards only the trailing component; TOCTOU remains on intermediate components — openat-per-component is the correct shape
